speakers: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
Moritz Seibert (Tuck A Capital CTA, guest host; caption "Tuck A Capital")
summary: Top Traders Unplugged Systematic Investor Ep.401 (May 2026): Moritz Seibert hosts Goldman's Nick Baltas on the QIS industry (macro views via systematic wrappers, crowding vs risk premia, WSJ article), the 2026 commodity curve carry drawdown after the March oil supply shock, trend following in 2026 (benchmark markets strong, alternative markets lagging), execution/slippage and single-stock trend vs momentum. Conclusion: premium-based strategies draw down on their known risks, diversify premia and allocate strategically rather than reactively.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: I think the whole QIS space has become a vehicle of expressing specific macro views, frankly speaking.
claims.claim: QIS has shifted from designing an uncorrelated return stream atop SAA to expressing macro views (long equities, long oil, short bonds) through systematic wrappers.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert (Tuck A Capital CTA, guest host; caption "Tuck A Capital")
claims.quote: there's the big event coming up with SpaceX, um which will probably increase that concentration quite a bit
claims.claim: The SpaceX IPO would increase S&P concentration, which already sits in a few Magnificent Seven stocks.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: You know, we're kind of pricing in rate cuts and now we're kind of debating how many of rate hikes we're going to see.
claims.claim: 2026 theme shifted from AI capex boosting profits to a geopolitical shock in March (Middle East) and a pivot from pricing rate cuts to debating hikes, reviving 2022 memories.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: Is it going to start impacting how, you know, equity and bond correlation plays out?
claims.claim: Sticky inflation could change stock-bond correlation, with inflation as the central theme and equity hedging at times.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: Typically, you see a fast way down and a bit more of a um kind of slow recovery. It was the other way around.
claims.claim: The March 2026 V-shape was unusual: a slow drop over weeks followed by a very quick recovery.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: if there is a risk-off mindset, you'll see more of a defensive tilting
claims.claim: QIS demand follows macro mood: risk-off brings defensive tilting; recovery or normalisation brings volatility selling and carry.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: you would see a bit more volatility selling, maybe some carry trades
claims.claim: In recovery or normalisation mindsets investors add volatility selling and carry trades.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: Okay, long vol was not a defensive trade at least for this market. Let's go back into trend following
claims.claim: Investors rotate defensive products reactively (trend after 2018, long vol after 2018/2020, back to trend after 2022), an 'act of regret' that is unhealthy for product design.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: it's not let's let's follow what did well yesterday, but rather let's kind of take a step back, see what we're solving for, and and and strategically kind of allocate to it.
claims.claim: Allocate strategically to what you are solving for rather than chasing what did well last.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert (Tuck A Capital CTA, guest host; caption "Tuck A Capital")
claims.quote: career risk is the is a key consideration here that is not easily quantifiable
claims.claim: Career risk pushes investors toward reactive allocation.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert (Tuck A Capital CTA, guest host; caption "Tuck A Capital")
claims.quote: the overall size of the QIS space is now about 1 trillion and about 3 trillion
claims.claim: QIS is about $1 trillion (about $3 trillion with leverage); JPM QIS revenue is up 30% year to date and GSAM runs about $175 billion in QIS.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: those profiles can be delivered in a call option in a in a capital protected structure in an OTC swap
claims.claim: Banks deliver systematic exposure in many wrappers (swaps, notes, options, capital protected), making access easy.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert (Tuck A Capital CTA, guest host; caption "Tuck A Capital")
claims.quote: In practice many bank QIS offerings look very similar if not identical and they often they often provide overlapping exposures.
claims.claim: Crowding and synchronised positioning in QIS: overlapping offerings can reduce profit potential.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: they should account for incremental flows into a specific premium or um you know overlap of positions between different strategies
claims.claim: Designers should look at aggregate flow into a premium and overlap across strategies, not each strategy in isolation, and monitor whether market depth can absorb the demand.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: anything that has excess demand can lead to subdued returns
claims.claim: Any strategy with excess demand (QIS, private equity, discretionary concentration) can see subdued returns; part of QIS flow is replacement of CTA flows, not new money.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert (Tuck A Capital CTA, guest host; caption "Tuck A Capital")
claims.quote: when you look at some of these, say, more niche QIS strategies, say, liquidity provision to the Beacon or GSCI roll window, maybe there is some decay that you can spot.
claims.claim: Niche QIS strategies such as GSCI roll-window liquidity provision may show return decay from too much money.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: there is an arbitrage that you know, shouldn't be there. It is purely a consequence of supply and demand imbalance.
claims.claim: Roll-window strategies harvest a supply/demand imbalance that should not exist, so more capital erodes the return, unlike risk-premium strategies.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: nobody could argue that not being on the side of the insurer is now a um if you like a a non-rewarded trade.
claims.claim: Selling volatility earns a risk premium because investors are risk-averse (concave utility); crowding may reduce its magnitude but not eliminate it.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: the crowding argument is perhaps an input into the time variation of risk premia
claims.claim: Crowding drives time variation in premia but not elimination; if a strategy captures a real risk its reward should be non-negative more often than not.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert (Tuck A Capital CTA, guest host; caption "Tuck A Capital")
claims.quote: These funds try to act before the QAS programs can resulting in a cat and mouse game that can cause unusual movements in various investments.
claims.claim: Quoted claim that hedge funds front-run QIS trades; Nick says index details are IP and the claim is unproven.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: this is about rolling commodity futures exposures on the back end of the curve and shorting the front.
claims.claim: Commodity curve carry rolls the back of the curve and shorts the front, capturing the differential roll yield (contango front is expensive); a carry trade.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: you are exposed to what we call uh shifting to a backwardation
claims.claim: Primary risk of curve carry is a supply shock shifting the front into backwardation as spot rallies.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: the situation in the Middle East um and the Strait of Hormuz and all that lot, uh the price of oil, as you just said, Moritz, uh skyrocketed
claims.claim: The March 2026 oil spike from Strait of Hormuz disruption (near-record WTI/Brent backwardation) and January natural gas cold-weather demand drove curve carry drawdowns.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: let's say for the last 40 years
claims.claim: The 2026 curve carry drawdown (~10% in simple implementations) was the worst in 40 years of data, roughly double the previous worst in 2018 (natural gas shock).

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: the drawdown came from a very well understood move that in itself is the number one risk factor when it comes to a curve carry trade
claims.claim: The drawdown came from the known primary risk, so it supports a risk premium rather than a broken strategy; drawdowns historically come from weather shocks, outages or geopolitics.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: whereas now, because you're rolling out of the current contract, you're almost crystallizing the negative P&L.
claims.claim: In 2022 a lower price allowed recovery, but in 2026 rolling out of the current contract crystallised the negative P&L.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: the benefit of having diversifying sources of return in a portfolio context allows you to weather quite well the period through March
claims.claim: Diversifying premia (other commodity strategies) helped investors absorb the curve carry drawdown, and the market reaction was calmer than in past years.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: We know what we're exposed to. The ultimate risk is realizing.
claims.claim: Clients accept known risk because they are harvesting a premium in the medium term; recovery in prices would help both roll yield and spot.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: a recovery phase which would bring prices down will make the strategy benefiting from it
claims.claim: In the short term risk remains because oil is news-driven, but a price decline would benefit curve carry through both yield and spot.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: There are implementations that beta hedge the front of the back.
claims.claim: Implementation matters: beta-hedging the front, dynamically selecting the back or closing the spread in backwardation reduced losses, and some variants were positive year to date.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: you know the news is driving the price more so than the supply demand dynamics.
claims.claim: Oil in 2026 moved on news more than supply-demand fundamentals.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert (Tuck A Capital CTA, guest host; caption "Tuck A Capital")
claims.quote: I mean, if there is a complete crisis and people are like just scrambling for barrels and there's this massive supply shock and we don't have enough going around, the front can be bid up.
claims.claim: Backwardation can widen further in a supply crisis, shown by logistics workarounds to bypass Hormuz (trains, trucks, East-West pipeline).

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: it's a good question whether the market can absorb the shortage
claims.claim: Economies adapt to lower supply, so the shortage effect is not static and hard to quantify.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: hasn't been a specific good period for for that part
claims.claim: In 2026 conventional benchmark markets outperformed in trend following, while non-benchmark commodities were poor for trend but good for reversion and skewness premia.
claims.indicator: trend in alternative vs benchmark markets

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: if you start looking into different premium like reversion or skewness dynamics, the exact opposite.
claims.claim: Diversification across premia (trend, reversion, skew) works across markets, with reversion winning where trend lagged.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: I really remember a period whereby all four major asset classes have been contributing positively.
claims.claim: In 2026 YTD equities, dollar, energy and rates all contributed to trend returns (straight-line commodities, rates trend since March, first time since 2022); economic trend signals, carry and reversion also added.
claims.indicator: trend by asset class, economic trends, carry, reversion
claims.direction: long equities, short dollar, short bonds, long commodities

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: stylistically solving for defensiveness, somebody should go with a core market universe because all you're trying to achieve is the principal component moves.
claims.claim: For defensiveness choose a core universe; for the best long-term risk-adjusted return go broader at some cost to defensiveness.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert (Tuck A Capital CTA, guest host; caption "Tuck A Capital")
claims.quote: you have that positive skew defensive especially during equity drawdowns, your long-term expected sharp ratio and performance potential is maximized more when you add all these alternative markets
claims.claim: Man AHL paper: concentrated macro portfolios give positive skew in equity drawdowns, while adding alternative markets maximises long-term Sharpe via idiosyncratic bets.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert (Tuck A Capital CTA, guest host; caption "Tuck A Capital")
claims.quote: There are some CTAs out there trading concentrated portfolios that are up 50%. Some are up 100%.
claims.claim: In 2026 concentrated CTAs in metals and energy were up 50-100% while broad-universe managers lagged because smaller markets dragged.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert (Tuck A Capital CTA, guest host; caption "Tuck A Capital")
claims.quote: that by no means says anything about what will happen next month
claims.claim: Hindsight shows concentrated portfolios did better in 2026 but that implies nothing about the future.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: There is no execution alpha that in itself will become part of the return.
claims.claim: In QIS execution is passive: the bank guarantees reference prices (closing or TWAP) and bears execution risk, so there is no execution alpha for clients.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert (Tuck A Capital CTA, guest host; caption "Tuck A Capital")
claims.quote: Now, if you trade at a different level to that price, that is slippage and that positive or negative slippage, you can be either direction, is on the books of Goldman Sachs
claims.claim: In QIS slippage versus index price stays with the bank, while in a CTA it flows directly to the client's P&L.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert (Tuck A Capital CTA, guest host; caption "Tuck A Capital")
claims.quote: They have different settlement procedures, different settlement windows, you know, different periods of time.
claims.claim: Execution should be market-specific because order books, settlement windows and liquidity concentration differ (for example Brazilian vs CME live cattle).

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert (Tuck A Capital CTA, guest host; caption "Tuck A Capital")
claims.quote: they have a more kind of like patient approach to getting into the trade. They're not forcing themselves to immediately transact and consume liquidity from the order book.
claims.claim: Gresham reports near-nil slippage in small markets through patient execution research; without it, slippage would cost two or three percent per year.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: one is very similar to the other plus some market timing mechanism
claims.claim: Time-series trend and cross-sectional momentum in single stocks are sister implementations of the same premium, the former adding market timing (Jegadeesh and Goyal).

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
claims.quote: allocating between value and quality and growth and so on and so forth on the basis of the relative momentum
claims.claim: Factor momentum is trend following at the factor level, an indirect single-stock expression, popularised by slow-moving ETF flows.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert (Tuck A Capital CTA, guest host; caption "Tuck A Capital")
claims.quote: That's an incorrect benchmark for a long short strategy
claims.claim: Comparing long-short strategies (and trend) to the S&P 500 is an incorrect benchmark.
